chunks: For each joint of the finger, one-third of the compensation of that finger applies, except the thumb; for he used to judge regarding each of its joints with one-half of the compensation of that thumb, because it has two joints.
Sahl ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Zarif, from his father Zarif ibn Nasih, who said: A man called Abdullah ibn Ayyub narrated to me; he said: Abu Amr al-Mutatabbib narrated to me; he said:

I presented this narration to Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, and he said: 'Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام gave a legal ruling, so the people wrote down his ruling, and Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام wrote it to his governors and the heads of his armies. Among what it contained was: If the upper eyelid is injured and split, then its compensation is one-third of the indemnity of the eye: one hundred dinars and sixty-six dinars and two-thirds of a dinar. If the lower eyelid is injured and split, then its compensation is half of the indemnity of the eye: two hundred and fifty dinars. And if the eyebrow is injured and all its hair is lost, then its compensation is half of the indemnity of the eye: two hundred and fifty dinars. So whatever of it is injured is according to that proportion.'

key_terms.الْإِبْهَامَ: the thumb, treated differently because it has two joints
key_terms.شُفْرُ الْعَيْنِ: the eyelid margin of the eye
key_terms.عَقْلِ: financial indemnity or compensation due for bodily injury
key_terms.فُتْيَاهُ: his legal ruling or juridical decision
key_terms.مَفْصِلٍ: joint of a finger or limb for which compensation is assessed

ai.seo_question: What compensation did أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام rule for injuries to finger joints, eyelids, and the eyebrow?
ai.summary: This report records legal rulings on bodily indemnities attributed to أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام and affirmed by Imam Abu Abdillah عليه السلام. It specifies proportional compensation for finger joints, the eyelids, and the eyebrow, showing a precise jurisprudential framework for bodily injury and retaliation.
